title: autotune: default batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: provide safe, production-ready defaults and tooling to automatically tune batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles for common workloads and expose unit-economics insights to operators. This change implements: 1) a new 'autotune' defaults layer that derives batching and cache TTL defaults from model profiles + observed request distributions; 2) a set of curated quantization profiles and a stable selection heuristic tied to latency and quality SLOs; 3) a small CLI and internal API for unit-economics (UEcon) queries and recommendations; 4) migration logic for existing customer configs so defaults opt-in on deploy; 5) dashboards and docs for operator workflows. The description below contains the checklist we used and a short rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] implement autotune defaults engine and schema - [x] add quantization profiles + selection heuristic - [x] expose UEcon CLI and server endpoint (internal) - [x] add metrics (uecon.*) and dashboards - [x] migration script and opt-in flag - [x] docs and example configs Rollout plan: stage feature behind feature-flag; enable for internal canary traffic for 48h; evaluate token-cost and latency regressions; opt-in customers via console toggle; full rollout after 2 weeks of canary stability. Related linear tasks: ENG-8421 (autotune engine), PM-318 (product acceptance criteria).
commits: feat(autotune): add defaults engine and schema (autotune/defaults.py)
feat(quant): add curated quantization profiles + selection heuristic (runtime/quant_profiles.go)
feat(uecon): add CLI + internal API for unit-econ queries (tools/uecon/cli.py, api/uecon/handler.go)
chore(docs): add docs + example configs for autotune and uecon (docs/uecon.md)
fix(migration): migration script to backfill missing config keys (scripts/migrate_autotune.py)
files_changed: runtime/autotune/defaults.py -- new module: core logic to compute batch_size, max_latency_target_ms, cache_ttl based on model_profile + observed qps distribution
runtime/quant/quant_profiles.go -- new profiles and selection logic (safety checks to avoid regressions)
api/uecon/handler.go -- internal-only HTTP endpoint to query cost/loss estimates per route/model
tools/uecon/cli.py -- interactive CLI to surface recommendations and run quick sims
scripts/migrate_autotune.py -- idempotent migration that backfills new keys and sets feature-flag false by default
docs/operations/uecon.md -- operator guide + dashboard links + runbook
dashboard/templates/uecon.json -- grafana template for UEcon metrics
review_comments: Miguel Torres (review): important change — can we make the default cache_ttl conservative for low-throughput routes? suggestion: derive a per-route floor from historical per-route median session length.
Aisha Kumar (author reply): agree — added a conservative floor computation and unit test. See defaults.py: compute_floor_from_history() and tests/test_defaults_floor.py
Priya Patel (review): quant profiles look good; please add a guard so operators can pin model to non-quantized profile even when autotune recommends quantization.
Aisha Kumar (author reply): added allowlist and console toggle; selection heuristic respects explicit profile pinning. Updated migration to not override existing pinned configs.
Ethan Zhang (review): CI flake on e2e related to a timing tolerance — looks unrelated but please rerun CI after fixing the test tolerance.
Aisha Kumar (author reply): fixed timing tolerance in tests/serve_integration_test.py and retriggered CI.

release_notes:
- Add autotune defaults engine for batching and cache TTLs
- Curated quantization profiles with safe selection heuristic
- Internal unit-economics CLI and API + Grafana dashboard template
- Migration script (opt-in by default) and operator docs
- No breaking changes; operators can pin profiles to opt-out of recommendations
